why: Top-p 0.95 at T 1.0 deletes the diffuse tail that holds the progress steps, lowering the cued base's text surprise below its optimum and bringing back some loops, so it loses about 12 of 410.

Min-p 0.1 cuts the tail hardest exactly at flat (impasse) positions where progress mass is spread over many paraphrases, so it sharpens toward the restatement more than top-p 0.95 does and costs the cued base about 20 points.

The truncated sampler pushes the cued base back toward the low-surprise trap, where restated blocks self-reinforce, so rule-A loops return from 0 at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 to a few tens (still well below the 71 at T 0.6).
Loops that self-reinforce run to the cap, so cap hits rise from 27 at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 by roughly the number of returned loops plus drift cases.

T 1.5 raises surprise and min-p 0.1 removes the incoherent tail, and the two roughly cancel near the cued base's optimum, so accuracy is close to the T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 cell rather than collapsing as T 1.5 alone would.
RL has concentrated the progress mass at forks, so tail truncation removes almost nothing it uses and its score stays at its temperature-invariant 463.
At T 1.0 the plain base is in the confusion trap: much of its text drifts and never reaches a clean final answer, so a large share of its 276 wrong answers have no extractable answer.
At T 0.6 the plain base is near its optimum, and its unextractable answers are mainly its 65-69 loop or cap hits plus a few format failures, far fewer than at T 1.0.
